investigation.answer: Telnet (TCP/23) is reachable from outside on site-b GigabitEthernet0/0/0 (ACL 3000, default permit - no deny for telnet) and core GigabitEthernet0/0 (no inbound ACL, all interfaces permit). site-a GigabitEthernet0/0 (ACL EDGE-IN) correctly denies telnet.
investigation.request: Fix the edge ACLs on site-b, core: telnet must be blocked

intent.summary: Remediate inbound ACLs on site-b and core to deny telnet (tcp/23).

diffs.site-b:
--- running
+++ candidate
@@ -12,4 +12,5 @@
  rule 5 permit tcp destination-port eq 443
  rule 10 deny tcp destination-port eq 445
+ rule 15 deny tcp destination-port eq 23
 #
 interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0
diffs.core:
--- running
+++ candidate
@@ -6,7 +6,12 @@
 interface GigabitEthernet0/0
  description UPLINK
+ ip access-group ACL-IN-GigabitEthernet0/0 in
 !
 router ospf 1
  network 10.0.0.0 0.0.255.255 area 0
 !
+ip access-list extended ACL-IN-GigabitEthernet0/0
+ 10 deny tcp any any eq 23
+ 20 permit ip any any
+!
 end

findings.matched: no rule matched: Huawei traffic-filter default permit
no inbound ACL applied on any interface

result.explanation:
site-b (huawei_vrp): adds rule 15 deny tcp dst-port 23 to existing ACL.
core (cisco_ios): creates ACL-IN-GigabitEthernet0/0 (10 deny tcp any any eq 23, 20 permit ip any any) bound inbound on GigabitEthernet0/0.
NOT touched: only audit-flagged interfaces changed; ssh/dns/http/ntp/snmp/bgp/https/rdp/ping verified unchanged.
Risk: MEDIUM - new inbound filter bound to core Gi0/0 plus rule additions on both devices.

reasons: core: new inbound filter bound to GigabitEthernet0/0
